content:
I just ran into this:

import Mathlib

-- ok
example : @RingCon.hasNSMul._aux_1 = @RingCon.instAddMonoidQuotient._aux_3 := rfl

-- fails
example : @RingCon.hasNSMul._aux_1 = @RingCon.instAddMonoidQuotient._aux_3 := by
  with_reducible_and_instances rfl

Both of these are providing the NSMul field, but since this is being abstracted by inferInstanceAs in two separate places, it ends up not reducibly defeq.
@Jovan Gerbscheid, do I remember correctly that you planned to replace the nsmul field with toNSMul : SMul Nat A which I think would fix this (or allow fast_instance% to)?

Replacing nsmul with a typeclass would definitely be a good idea, but I think the issue is deeper than that in this corner of the library. Look at

import Mathlib

example {R : Type*} [Ring R] (c : RingCon R) :
    (RingCon.hasZSMul c : SMul ℤ c.Quotient) = RingCon.instSMulQuotient c := by
  with_reducible_and_instances rfl -- fails

The issue is that the Z-action is declared under some assumptions and the general SMul is declared under another set of assumptions (which does not imply the former). Moreover, both actions are behind opaque functions provided by inferInstanceAs.

I see two solutions here:
(1): declare the Z-action only under stronger assumptions (assuming R is a ring), as a special case of the general SMul action.
(2): don't use inferInstanceAs and make the constructions reducible enough that Lean can see the actions are the same.

(1) feels more natural to me, because I would think that RingCon is designed for rings, but I'm probably missing some applications (the file is careful to build things for NonUnitalNonAssocCommSemiring and friends). So (2) is maybe safer. Thoughts?
Minimally invasive fix at #40704: I define there all the SMul through the same function, so they are reducibly defeq by design.

I indeed have a PR that adds an NSMul type class for the nsmul field, but I haven't quite convinced myself that this change is worth the minor slowdown that it causes. In particular, for the issue you describe with inferInstanceAs, it is supposed to be able to handle that correctly with the current setup.

I have realized that there are other places in Mathlib where this is an issue. #40706 fixes the ones I've noticed.

There are two issues here. The first one is that generic SMul definitions should be located before the definitions that could use it like AddMonoid or AddGroup. The second one is that, since this is an nsmul field and not a class field, inferInstanceAs has no reason to try to use the generic SMul, so we should provide it by hand.

The first one has to be fixed in any case. For the second one, introducing an NSMul typeclass would make it be handled automatically by inferInstanceAs, while for now we have to be careful.
Iirc SplittingField suffers from the same diamonds, and it is not entirely trivial to fix it there.
Good catch. I'm proposing a fix in #40708, along the same lines as what I've done above.

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

Minimally invasive fix at #40704: I define there all the SMul through the same function, so they are reducibly defeq by design.

I should probably have clarified that I already had essentially this fix, and rather was wondering if this should be considered a bug in inferInstanceAs.

If we define some structure like AddMonoid that needs some SMul, and then later we define a general SMul that specializes to the one used in AddMonoid, I don't see how inferInstanceAs could guess what we want. In this case, I'd say the issue is on our side, and we should move the SMul instance before the AddMonoid.

Definitely SMul should come earlier, but that doesn't help without also promoting the nsmul field from a function to a typeclass instance. I don't think a new NSMul typeclass would help much, since here we need an automatic instance from SMul but everywhere else we need the instance the other way
In #38036 I have added the NSMul type class, which lets inferInstanceAs use SMul instances for the nsmul field.

I think #38036 is a very good idea, and that we should go for it even if there is a small performance penalty, because it removes a footgun that is very hard to notice for non-experts (and even for experts :-)

Indeed there you add the instance in both directions:

@[default_instance high, to_additive toSMul]
instance NPow.toPow {M : Type*} [NPow M] : Pow M ℕ :=
  ⟨fun x n ↦ NPow.npow n x⟩

@[to_additive ofSMul]
instance NPow.ofPow {M : Type*} [Pow M ℕ] : NPow M := ⟨fun n x ↦ Pow.pow x n⟩
I would guess that using [toNSMul : SMul Nat A] inside addMonoid is more performant, since unification would not need to unfold these instances

My motivation for not doing that is that we can continue to write nsmul := ... when declaring instances.

Also I'm not sure whether inferInstanceAs would support that construction - it might only go into parents that are given by extends.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

My motivation for not doing that is that we can continue to write nsmul := ... when declaring instances.

Do we do this very frequently? toNSMul := .nsmulRec could be made to work, and in other cases I would guess it's better to define a more general smul separately.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

My motivation for not doing that is that we can continue to write nsmul := ... when declaring instances.

Also I'm not sure whether inferInstanceAs would support that construction - it might only go into parents that are given by extends.

This sounds possible, but also arguably like it should be considered a bug.
Why do we need a new NSMul typeclass instead of just doing extends toSMulNat : SMul Nat alpha?
You can't also extend the Int version because the smul fields clash
I thought that's what renaming was for?
Does that exist again?
We had it in lean 3

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

(1) feels more natural to me, because I would think that RingCon is designed for rings

No! docs#RingCon exists precisely to be used for semirings, where it is a better notion than that of (two-sided) ideal.
